The BHRC expects any new Executive Director to be engaged on terms that are consistent with the policy. However, it recognizes that it cannot anticipate
circumstances in which any new Executive Director may be recruited. The Committee may determine that it is in the interests of the Company and shareholders
to secure the services of a particular individual which may require it to take account of the terms of that individual’s existing employment and/or their personal
circumstances.
Accordingly, the BHRC will ensure that:
• The salary level of any new Executive Director is appropriate to their role and the competitive environment at the time of appointment. Where appropriate
it may appoint an individual on a lower salary, then gradually increase salary levels as the individual gains experience in the role.
• Variable remuneration will be awarded within the parameters of the policy.
• The BHRC would expect any new Executive Director to participate in the Company pension and benefit schemes that are open to other senior employees
but would take into account the Executive Director’s existing arrangements and market norms.
• Where an individual is relocating in order to take up the role, the Company may provide certain one-off benefits such as reasonable relocation expenses,
accommodation for a period of time following appointment, assistance with visa applications or other immigration issues and ongoing arrangements such
as tax equalization, annual flights home and a housing allowance.
• Where an individual would be forfeiting remuneration or employment terms in order to join the Company, the BHRC may at its discretion award appropriate
compensation. The BHRC would require reasonable evidence of the nature and value of any forfeited arrangements and would, to the extent practicable,
ensure any compensation was of comparable commercial value and capped as appropriate, taking into account the terms of the previous arrangement
being forfeited (for example the form and structure of award, timeframe, performance criteria and likelihood of vesting). Where appropriate, the BHRC would
have a preference for buy-outs to be delivered in the form of cash.
In making any decision on the remuneration of a new Executive Director, the BHRC would balance shareholder expectations, current best practice and the
circumstances of any new Executive Director. It would strive not to pay more than is necessary to recruit the right candidate and would give full details in the
next remuneration report.
Note: At present there is only one Executive Director namely the Group Managing Director (GMD).
